timing.note: only 2 fully-covered eclipse(s) in the data - at least 3 are needed to test the period for timing changes

writeup: TIC 333952894 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 0.6611 days, detected in TESS photometry with a primary eclipse depth of 8.70 percent dimming. The automated pipeline identified this signal with a Box Least Squares significance of 586.1, and difference imaging analysis yielded a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 85.8. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, a critical limitation affects this result: the centroid of the dimming signal lies only 0.022 pixels closer to the target star than to a nearby bright neighbor, a margin well within TESS's stated centroid systematic uncertainty of 0.10 to 0.3 pixels. This means the available data cannot confidently distinguish whether the signal originates from TIC 333952894 or from the nearby star. No secondary eclipse was detected.
